bib.title: World Model on Million-Length Video And Language With Blockwise RingAttention

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "World Model on Million-Length Video and Language with Blockwise RingAttention" (LWM), Hao Liu*, Wilson Yan*, Matei Zaharia, Pieter Abbeel (UC Berkeley). ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2402.08268v4, 3 Feb 2025). Venue per the header: "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025".

COVERAGE: All 64,310 chars were extracted. I read the full text through the main body, limitations, hyperparameter tables, and Appendices A-D. For the rest of the appendix (E onward) I read the start and checked the end: it is qualitative image, video-understanding and generation examples (Fig 14-18 and later), with no result tables. The reference list was skimmed. Figures were not rendered. The figures.py captions run printed nothing I could use, so captions below come from the extracted text. Page numbers are approximate. The note 03-budgeting-the-window.md showed no existing mention of this paper (grep found nothing).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Naive needle-in-a-haystack retrieval is near-perfect at 1M tokens, but harder multi-needle retrieval degrades; the authors say 1M context is still under-used.
  number: LWM-Text-1M at 1M: 0.67 / 0.84 / 0.69 for (N=2,R=2), (N=4,R=1), (N=4,R=2). At 32K the same model scores 0.84 / 0.97 / 0.84.
  setup: 7B LLaMA-2-based model; magic-number-per-city needles; N is the number of needles and R the number to retrieve. Scoring is string match (App. D).
  quote: "we note that we see degradation in accuracy while increasing the difficulty of the needle retrieval task, suggesting that there is still more room to improve on the 1M context utilization of our model."
  where: Sec 3.3.3 and Table 2, p.5-6.
- Claim: Other 7B models given 1M context through positional extrapolation collapse on multi-needle retrieval. These were run after the paper was completed.
  number: Table 2 rows at 1M, N=2,R=2 / N=4,R=1 / N=4,R=2: Llama-3.1-8B 0.27/0.32/0.18; Qwen2.5-7B 0.0/0.0/0.0; Mistral-7B-v0.3 0.05/0.13/0.10; LWM 0.67/0.84/0.69. GPT-4-1106 at 128K: 0.92/0.8/0.82.
  setup: Rows marked * were added after paper completion. GPT-4 and Gemini Pro have "-" at 1M.
  quote: "Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct* 0.0 0.0 0.0" and "LWM-Text-1M (Ours) 0.67 0.84 0.69"
  where: Table 2, p.6.
- Claim: Tuning the chat/retrieval training mix trades chat quality against needle retrieval accuracy. This is useful for the "more context is not free" argument.
  number: Chat/QA mix 0/100 gives MT-Bench 2.42, needle 100%. 70/30 gives 4.62, 96%. 90/10 gives 5.1, 55%. 100/0 gives 5.8, 31%.
  setup: LWM-Text-Chat, MT-Bench and needle accuracy; training-data mix ablation.
  quote: "Needle Retrieval accuracy decreases, suggesting a trade-off where increasing chat interaction capabilities may reduce the system's precision in retrieving specific information or 'needles' from input context."
  where: App. B.2, Table 11, p.17.
- Claim: A 512K-context LWM beats 128K-context GPT-4o and 200K-context Claude 3 Opus on three LOFT tasks (retrieval-in-context and RAG-style). The gap is largest on HotPotQA.
  number: Quora 0.38 / 0.23 / 0.37; NQ 0.37 / 0.22 / 0.37; HotPotQA 0.72 / 0.21 / 0.32 (LWM-512K / GPT-4o-128K / Claude 3 Opus-200K).
  setup: LOFT corpus holds thousands of documents in context. The model returns doc ids (Quora, HotPotQA) or answers with context (NQ). Each model was run at its own context length, so the 512K LWM sees more of the corpus than the 128K GPT-4o.
  quote: "HotPotQA 0.72 0.21 0.32"
  where: Table 3, p.6.
- Claim: Long video understanding. LWM-1M handles up to about 1800 frames, but trails newer larger or proprietary models on Video-MME.
  number: Medium (4-15 min) / Long (30-60 min): LWM-1M 63.7 / 60.8; Gemini 1.5 Pro* 74.3 / 67.4; GPT-4o* 70.3 / 65.3; LLaVA-Video* 68.9 / 61.5; Long-LLaVA 7B 51.4 / 45.4; Video-LLaVA 7B (8 frames) 38.1 / 36.2.
  setup: Video-MME. LWM uses 256 VQGAN tokens per frame. * marks models released after the paper.
  quote: "LWM-1M 7B ≤ 1800 63 .7 60 .8"
  where: Table 4, p.8.
- Claim: Fixed small frame budgets (temporal subsampling) lose fine-grained information. Long context lets the model attend to thousands of frames.
  number: Video-LLaVA is restricted to 8 frames.
  quote: "Video-LLaV A (Lin et al., 2023) is restricted to uniformly sampling 8 frames from a video, no matter how long the original video may be."
  where: Sec 4.3.1, p.8.
- Claim: Context cost in tokens. Each video frame costs 256 tokens, so about 1M tokens covers ~1 hour of video.
  number: 256 tokens per frame (16x16 VQGAN codes from 256x256 images). Demos are 1-hour videos.
  quote: "Each video frame is tokenized into 256 tokens using VQGAN"
  where: Fig 3 caption, p.3. Frame budget is inferred from Table 4 "≤ 1800" frames and the 1-hour demos, and the paper does not state the arithmetic.
- Claim: Context extension did not hurt short-context benchmarks, except MMLU at 512K and 1M.
  number: MMLU 0.39 (Llama-2 4K) / 0.41 (128K) / 0.36 (512K) / 0.35 (1M). HellaSwag acc 0.57 across all variants.
  quote: "mmlu 0.39 0.4 0.41 0.41 0.36 0.35"
  where: Table 1, p.4. The text claims "absence of negative effects" and the MMLU drop at the longest stages contradicts that. Worth flagging.
- Claim: Progressive context extension is cheap relative to training at full length.
  number: Stages 32K/128K/256K/512K/1M use 4.8B/12B/12B/3B/1.8B tokens, taking 8h/45h/83h/47h/58h on TPU v4-512. RoPE theta goes 1M, 10M, 10M, 25M, 50M.
  setup: Initialized from LLaMA-2 7B and trained on Books3 filtered by document length. Each stage starts from the previous one.
  quote: "Total Tokens 4.8B 12B 12B 3B 1.8B"
  where: Table 6, p.16.
- Claim: Serving a 1M-token context needs a large TPU slice.
  number: Minimum v4-128, 32-way tensor parallel x 4-way sequence parallel (ring).
  setup: Single precision; no quantization.
  quote: "Inference for such long sequences requires a minimum of v4-128 with a TPU mesh sharding of 32 tensor parallelism, and 4 sequence parallelism (ring dimension)."
  where: App. A, p.15.
- Claim: Sequence packing must mask attention across packed examples and reweight the loss, or image-understanding accuracy drops.
  number: Standard packing vs masked packing: VQA v2 48.3 vs 55.8; SQA 34.8 vs 47.7; POPE 62.5 vs 75.2.
  quote: "Standard independent packing 48.3 34.8 62.5" / "Masked sequence packing (Ours) 55.8 47.7 75.2"
  where: Table 9, p.17.
- Claim: Synthetic long-context QA training data is made by chunking books and having a short-context model write a Q/A pair per chunk. The question is placed at the end of the concatenated chunks, so the model must attend anywhere in the context.
  number: 1,000-token chunks; chat mix about 7:3 UltraChat to QA; loss tokens <1% per QA sequence.
  quote: "split documents from the Books3 dataset into fixed chunks of 1,000 tokens"
  where: Sec 3.2, p.4.
- Claim: Compute-overlap point. With enough tokens per device, Blockwise RingAttention's communication is fully hidden by computation, so context scales with device count without approximation.
  quote: "the communication cost during sequence parallelism is fully overlapped by computation, resulting in no additional overhead."
  number: none
  where: Sec 3.1, p.3.

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Conclusion): vanilla frame-by-frame tokenization ignores temporal redundancy, with no continuous CLIP embeddings. Quote: "Our models use more tokens per parameter than Chinchilla's recommendation, but being much smaller than current large language models (100B+ parameters), our findings may not directly apply to them."
- Image and short-video benchmarks are below state of the art because of discrete VQGAN tokens (VQA v2 55.8 vs LLaVA-1.5 78.5).
- The paper concedes that retrieval is the main long-context test and that harder synthesis benchmarks are needed. It concedes multi-needle accuracy falls as difficulty rises.
- The longer chat models lose slightly on MT-Bench (1M 4.19 vs 256K 5.0), which the authors attribute to less training data on longer sequences. This is a hypothesis, not tested.
- The Table 2 comparisons mix eras. Gemini Pro and GPT-4 have no 1M entries, and the starred open models were run after the paper was finished.
- Dated: Gemini 1.5, GPT-4o and Claude 3 Opus are the 2024 baselines. The paper is a training recipe, not a prompting or budgeting study. It gives no cost or latency curves for inference, and no measurement of lost-in-the-middle (the Fig 2 and Fig 11 heatmaps are described as near-perfect only).
- Single-needle "near-perfect" is described in prose and figures only, with no table of values.

BUILDS ON
- Blockwise RingAttention (Liu, Zaharia, Abbeel 2024; Liu and Abbeel 2023).
- FlashAttention (Dao et al. 2022).
- RoPE (Su et al. 2024), with theta scaling following Code Llama (Rozière et al. 2023).
- Progressive length growth (Jin et al. 2023a, GrowLength).
- Llama 2 (Touvron et al. 2023b).
- VQGAN (Esser et al. 2021) via aMUSEd (Patil et al. 2024).
- Needle-in-a-Haystack (gkamradt 2023; ArizeAI 2023 variant).
- LOFT (Lee et al. 2024).
- Video-MME (Fu et al. 2024).
- Books3 / The Pile (Gao et al. 2020).
- UltraChat (Ding et al. 2023).
- Concurrent work: Gemini 1.5 (Reid et al. 2024).

CODE: none in the paper (code and models are linked at largeworldmodel.github.io/lwm/).

FIGURES
- Fig 1: context-size comparison of LLMs (p.1).
- Fig 2: needle retrieval versus Gemini Pro (32K) and GPT-4 (128K), with the x-axis log-scale to 128K and linear to 1M (p.2). It is the quickest view of the claim that the model matches the short-window models and extends 8x further.
- Fig 3: model architecture, 256 tokens per frame and the <vision>/<eof>/<eov> delimiters (p.3). It explains the per-frame token cost.
- Fig 4: training stages and data (p.4).
- Fig 5: multi-needle results for LWM-1M (p.5).
- Fig 6: 1-hour video QA against GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision (p.8).
- Fig 8: MFU per stage (p.15).
- Fig 11-13: single-needle heatmaps for the 1M, 256K and 512K chat models (p.18).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction is clean for text and tables, but the Table 4/5 columns run together, so the values were rechecked against the row text. Appendix A has a broken reference ("See Appendix ??"). Figures contain data that the text extraction cannot reach, such as the heatmaps. Title is dated 2024 in the filename, but the arXiv v4 and ICLR 2025 versions are what was read (arXiv:2402.08268).
